title: Chilli con Carne
subtitle: Slow-cooked beef and kidney bean chilli
excerpt: The Tex-Mex standard that has become a global comfort food: beef mince simmered low and slow with kidney beans, tinned tomatoes, and a careful blend of chilli and spices until the sauce is thick and deeply flavoured. Better the next day.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chilli con carne (chilli with meat) has its roots in the Spanish Colonial cooking of Texas and northern Mexico, where dried chillies were used to flavour tough cuts of meat. It was popularised across the United States in the late nineteenth century at chilli stands in San Antonio, Texas, and became an American staple. True Texan chilli (the competition style) uses chunks of beef rather than mince and contains no beans: beans are considered by many Texas chilli devotees to be an adulteration. The everyday domestic version with mince and kidney beans is derived from this but is a different dish; it is closer to the chilli that arrived in Britain with American diner culture in the mid-twentieth century and became a British takeaway and pub staple. The version here is the widely made domestic chilli: practical, accessible, and good. The spice blend should include both sweet and hot chilli, cumin, coriander, and a small amount of cinnamon.

content.text: Brown the mince properly in batches; crowding the pan steams the meat and prevents the colour that gives depth of flavour. The long simmer is not optional: 30 minutes of cooking produces an acceptable result; 90 minutes produces a good one. A small square of dark chocolate added at the end rounds the flavour without making it taste of chocolate.

Heat the oil in a large pan. Cook the onion and pepper for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Push to the side of the pan and increase the heat. Fry the mince in batches until deeply browned, breaking it up as it cooks. Add the tomato purée and spices and stir for 1 minute.

Add the tinned tomatoes, bay leaves, and 200 ml of water. Bring to a simmer, stirring to scrape up any browned bits. Season with salt. Reduce to a low simmer, partially cover, and cook for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.

Add the kidney beans and cook for a further 20 minutes uncovered until the sauce is thick. Stir in the dark chocolate until melted. Remove the bay leaves. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve with rice, soured cream, and coriander.
